2007 Y L R 1065

[Lahore]

Before Muhammad Jehangir Arshad, J

KHALID MEHMOOD---Petitioner

Versus

Mst. ANJUM FIRDOUS and others-Respondents

Writ Petition No.3446 of 2005, decided on. 21st
March, 2006.

West Pakistan Family Courts Act (XXXV of 1964)---

---S.5, Sched. & S.14---Constitution of Pakistan
(1973), Art.199---Constitutional petition---Suit for recovery of amount of
maintenance---Family Court dismissed suit for recovery of maintenance amount
filed by wife, but on appeal, Appellate Court set aside judgment of Family
Court and allowed the wife maintenance allowance at the rate of Rs.1000 per
month from the date of institution of the suit---Husband after obtaining
permission from Arbitration Council in terms of S.6 of Muslim Family Laws
Ordinance 1961, contracted second marriage and he was enjoying matrimonial life
having three children from his second wife; whereas the lady was being kept in
matrimonial bond without any reason--.-When suggested by High Court to counsel
for petitioner/husband whether he was ready to divorce the lady in lieu of
one-half of amount of maintenance decreed by
Appellate Court below from the date of institution of suit in lieu of
consideration of Khula; he consented with condition that amount of Rs.1000 per
month be reduced to Rs.800 per month---Said suggestion as well as request of
counsel for husband having been accepted by the lady constitutional petition
was disposed of accordingly.

Sardar Muhammad Iqbal Khakwani for Petitioner.

Shamsher Iqbal Chughtai for Respondent No. 1.

Date of hearing: 21st March, 2006.

JUDGMENT

MUHAMMAD JEHANGIR ARSHAD, J.---This writ
petition calls in question the judgment dated 15-6-2005 passed by learned
Additional District Judge, Ahmadpur East whereby the learned Additional
District Judge while "allowing appeal of Mst. Anjum Firdous respondent'
No.1 against the judgment and decree of the learned trial Court/Judge Family
Court dated 26-11-1997 dismissing suit of respondent No.1 for maintenance,
allowed her maintenance allowance at the rate of Rs.1,000 per month from the
date of institution of the suit.

2. Admittedly the parties are entangled in litigation
since 1997 to-date,' and in the meanwhile the petitioner after obtaining
permission from the Arbitration Council in terms of section 6 of the Muslim
Family Laws Ordinance dated 9-8-2000, against which the respondent No.1 filed
no revision, contracted second marriage and is now enjoying matrimonial life
begetting three children from his second wife, whereas Mst. Anjum Firdous
respondent No.1 is being kept in matrimonial bond without any reason,
therefore, when suggested by this Court to the learned counsel for the
petitioner, whether .the petitioner is ready to divorce respondent No.1 in lieu
of one-half of the amount of maintenance decreed by learned Additional District
Judge on 15-6-2005 from the date of institution of the suit in lieu of
consideration for Khula, the learned counsel in the presence of the petitioner
half-heartedly showed his consent with the request that maintenance allowance
as determined by the learned Additional District Judge at the rate of Rs.1,000
per month be reduced to Rs.800 per month. As the above suggestion as well as
the request of learned counsel for the petitioner is acceptable to Mst. Anjum
Firdous respondent No.1 present in Court along with her counsel, this writ
petition therefore, is disposed of in the following terms:

(i) The amount of
maintenance allowance as fixed by the learned Additional District Judge dated
15-6-2005 at the rate of Rs.1,000 per month is reduced to Rs.800 per month
payable by the petitioner to respondent No.1 from the date of institution of
the suit, till date;

(ii) The marriage between
the parties shall stand dissolved from today in lieu of surrender by Mst. Anjum
Firdous respondent No.1 her right of maintenance at the rate of Rs.400 per
month from the date of institution of the suit in lieu of consideration for
Khula; and

(iii) Mst. Anjum Firdous
respondent No.1 however, shall be entitled to recover the maintenance allowance
from the petitioner at the rate of Rs.400 per
month till 30-6-2006 viz. including the period of Iddat from today.

There is no order
as to costs.

H.B.T./K-3/L
Order accordingly.
